I'll analyze your spending to see if there are any concerns with how your agents are using their budgets.
**Your agents are mostly on track, but there are three things to fix:**

**1. Recover $0.80 from a dead intent (do this now)**
Your marketing tools trial ended and wasn't adopted. Intent `0xe88b02abd36a10617386cd71105ff39276ccdf16` still holds $0.80 that's serving no purpose. Withdraw it and put it back in your operating account.

**2. Raise the cloud infra cap this week (medium priority)**
Your cloud agent is **throttled**. Two consecutive payments to your infra provider each hit 98% of the $0.50 per-transaction ceiling — the agent has to split what looks like a ~$0.98 weekly bill into two transactions. The intent has room (`$2` total cap, only 49% used), so raise the per-transaction cap to $1.00 to let the agent pay cleanly in one go and reduce operational friction.

**3. Lock down the general ops intent before using it (monitor)**
Intent `0x568222982112b7bd55bd90524e1434472f422f5b` is Active with a $10 cap but has **no merchant allowlist** — meaning any address can receive funds. It's currently unfunded, but if you start using it, define which vendors this agent can actually pay first, then lock it in.

Your research subscription and marketing trial intents are fine. All payments are audited and under control.

data.headline: Revoke the idle marketing-trial intent to recover $0.80; raise the cloud-infra cap because payments are hitting 98% of perTxCap and throttling real spend.

findings.title: Idle capital locked in revoked intent
findings.detail: Intent 0xe88b02abd36a10617386cd71105ff39276ccdf16 (Marketing tools trial) is Revoked with $0.80 unspent funded balance. The trial ended and the tool was not adopted; this capital serves no purpose and should be recovered.
evidence: revokeReason: Trial ended, tool not adopted

findings.title: Cloud infra agent is throttled by undersized perTxCap
findings.detail: Intent 0x4e0866d3c7ac1acbd4058cc9a0877193e640bcf4 shows two consecutive payments to the same merchant (0x1111...1111), each hitting 98% of the $0.50 perTxCap. This is a classic throttling signal: the agent must split a $0.98 weekly bill into two transactions because the cap is too small. The totalCap ($2) has only 49% utilization but perTxCap is the binding constraint. Raising perTxCap will reduce payment fragmentation and operational friction.

findings.title: Unrestricted merchant allowlist on active discretionary intent
findings.detail: Intent 0x568222982112b7bd55bd90524e1434472f422f5b (General ops agent) is Active with a $10 totalCap and zero merchant restrictions (unrestrictedMerchants=true, merchantAllowlistSize=0). Although currently unfunded and unused, this configuration is a containment risk: if capital is added or the agent becomes active, any merchant can receive funds up to the cap with no audit trail constraint.

actions.rationale: Intent is revoked and trial is closed. Withdrawing $0.80 unspent funded balance eliminates idle capital and returns it to the payer's operating account.

Payments are hitting 98% of the $0.50 perTxCap; the merchant charges ~$0.98 per week and must split into two txs. Raise perTxCap to $1.0 to allow full weekly bills in one transaction and reduce fragmentation, while keeping totalCap at $2 as a safety bound.

Define an allowlist of approved merchants for this $10 discretionary intent. Unrestricted spend at this cap width creates uncontrolled exposure. Audit what vendors this agent legitimately needs to pay, then lock the allowlist before funding resumes.

dataGaps: Merchant names and categories are only addresses; cannot confirm whether 0x1111...1111 is actually a single cloud provider or multiple vendors
No intraday or historical trend data; cannot confirm whether the two 0.49 USDC cloud payments are a pattern or a one-time spike
Actual scheduled payment amounts from the cloud vendor are not provided; recommendation to raise perTxCap to $1.0 is based on observed spend, not on a vendor contract
